summaries.Good news: Today's uplifting stories celebrate human creativity and healing—from a teen uncovering lost history through mudlarking to a rescued gorilla becoming a mother in the wild, and hospitals redesigning their sonic environments to reduce patient stress. Real progress appears in music education reaching 20,000 students and a compound from pomegranates potentially transforming heart failure treatment.
summaries.Ideas: The day's thinking pieces grapple with AI's paradoxical popularity despite public skepticism, the need for better enterprise AI governance, and how creative disciplines like ballroom dance might counter dystopian narratives about technology's future. A new government 'Super Intelligence Force' signals shifting policy priorities around AI regulation.
summaries.Technology: From smart wallpaper generating electricity from indoor humidity to vehicle-to-grid systems that could stabilize power grids, today's innovations focus on sustainable energy solutions and human-centered interfaces—including a physical key that helps users reclaim screen time control. AI tooling dominates Product Hunt with agents, code review systems, and creative video generation.
summaries.Design: Design thinking expands into unexpected territories today: a remote 'knocker' device explores superstition through interaction, modular concrete furniture enables improvised public gathering, and a Vietnamese home proves that nature-integrated design creates living spaces that breathe. Plant-based materials innovation and adaptive building facades show design solving real systemic challenges.

items.title: Knocker device remotely "knocks on wood" to explore long-held superstition
